question.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cosecant function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsch}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-4\operatorname{arcsch}⁡{e}^{x}) \\  & =-4\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsch}⁡{e}^{x}) \\  & =-4\cdot (-\frac{1}{|{e}^{x}|\sqrt{1+{({e}^{x})}^{2}}})\cdot ({e}^{x})^{′} \\  & =4\cdot \frac{1}{{e}^{x}\cdot \sqrt{1+{e}^{2x}}}\cdot {e}^{x} \\  & =\frac{4}{\sqrt{1+{e}^{2x}}}.\end{aligned}
$$
